ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Sick Visit — Elvis Presley — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for low back pain

text.paragraph: Low back pain for two days after karate practice. [S]

Mr. Presley asked for a same-day visit. Two days ago, a week after returning from his Las Vegas engagement, he twisted while practicing karate and felt a sharp pain across the left lower back. The pain is worse when he bends, stands up from a chair or turns in bed, and eases lying on his side with heat. It does not go down his legs. He has no numbness, weakness, bladder or bowel change, numbness in the saddle area, fever or chills, and no history of cancer or injected drugs. He rates the pain 7 out of 10. He has taken his usual buprenorphine 16 mg each morning, no other opioid and no extra diazepam, and he is worried that the pain will make him want his old pills and that it will not settle before the tour in eighteen days. The prescription drug monitoring program shows only this clinic's prescriptions. [S]

list.item:
Acute low back strain (S39.012A). A muscular strain without radiculopathy or red flags; imaging would not help. Buprenorphine itself gives pain relief that lasts six to eight hours, so splitting the same daily dose is the first step; a full-agonist opioid is not added because he is in early recovery and it would compete with buprenorphine. A muscle relaxant is avoided because it would add sedation to diazepam and his sleep apnea. [S]
Take buprenorphine as one 8 mg film twice daily instead of 16 mg once, the same total.
Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food for five days; check home blood pressure.
Heat, gentle walking and staying active; no bed rest.
No imaging; physical therapy if not much better in two weeks.
Return at once for leg weakness, numbness, bladder or bowel change, or fever.

Opioid use disorder on buprenorphine (F11.20). Pain is a known trigger for cravings; he raised it himself, which is a strength. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; naloxone on hand. [S]
A phone check in three days.
Counseling session this week moved earlier.

Benzodiazepine use disorder on a diazepam taper (F13.20). No extra diazepam taken; no taper step during an acute illness. [S]
The next step will be decided at the ten-week review.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain — United States, 2022 (2022); The ASAM National Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Opioid Use Disorder: 2020 Focused Update (2020); Noninvasive Treatments for Acute, Subacute, and Chronic Low Back Pain: A Clinical Practice Guideline From the American College of Physicians (2017)

Follow-up: Phone check in three days. Ten-week review in two weeks, before the tour. Return sooner as above. Next scheduled visit 1974-09-23: ten-week review after the Las Vegas engagement and a back strain: buprenorphine, the taper, weight treatment, sleep apnea and planning for a three-week tour. [S]
